history.summary: NOT A TEMPLE - this is Parmarth Niketan, a Hindu ashram and spiritual retreat, the largest ashram in Rishikesh with over 1,000 rooms on an eight-acre campus on the banks of the Ganga at Swarg Ashram. Founded in 1942 by Pujya Swami Shukdevanandji Maharaj (1901-1965); since 1986 its president and spiritual head is Pujya Swami Chidanand Saraswatiji Maharaj, and Sadhvi Bhagawati Saraswati teaches there. Daily life includes yoga, meditation, morning universal prayers, satsang, kirtan, nature-cure and Ayurvedic treatment, and the famous sunset Ganga Aarti at its ghat. The campus includes a 14-ft Shiva statue on the riverbank and gardens for pilgrims from around the world. Documented as an ashram; keep-or-drop decision needed if the dataset is temples-only.

name: Parmarth Niketan
town_description: Rishikesh, the 'Yoga Capital of the World', sits on the Ganges in the foothills of the Himalayas in Uttarakhand, where the river leaves the mountains for the plains. Sacred to Hindus as the place of the sage Raibhya's penance, it is a centre of ashrams, yoga schools and the evening Ganga Aarti, and a gateway to the Char Dham pilgrimage. Parmarth Niketan lies in the Swarg Ashram quarter on the river's east bank.

visitor_information.opening_hours: The ashram is open daily; the Ganga Aarti is held at sunset (around 6:00 PM). Ashram accommodation requires prior booking; day visitors are welcome (verify current visitor policy).
